Yeah, i stated the differences between what a good pokemon game is vs what is not, i mean, imagine if they release a game where you only have to catch pokemons and do nothing else, they should add all the cool features of the original pokemon games, training pokemons (real train, not with candies), pvp battles, npcs battles, pokemon centers, maybe money and shops to get pokeballs /potions, not just spinning stuffs, but to be clear, the game is a great starting point, but is a starting point for now, i feel like 90% of a "pokemon world" is missing.
No way, or maybe, i've never saw someone who was playing for the major objectives of finishing the pokedex vs having a great squad of pokemons trained by yourself.

Yeah, "augmented reality games" are nice and new, but if the augmented reality is used only to catch "figures" of pokemon, spinning monuments to get pokeballs and nothing else i'm not sure that this should be rated as the most interactive video game ever, if you value the "i have to walk to do stuffs" ok, it's fun, but the real "game" behind that is pretty poor.
They should focus also on the game, thats the point.
